newsitem.title: USA: House clears way for Barshefsky as U.S. trade chief. [CORRECTED 23:22 GMT]
newsitem.headline: House clears way for Barshefsky as U.S. trade chief. [CORRECTED 23:22 GMT]

text.p: The House of Representatives voted on Tuesday to clear the way for Charlene Barshefsky to serve as U.S. Trade Representative.
By voice vote the House joined the Senate in approving a measure waiving a legal barrier against President Bill Clinton's nominee and sent it to the president to sign into law.
Barshefsky was expected to be sworn in soon.
The measure waived a law barring anyone who previously represented a foreign government in a trade dispute with the United States from occupying the trade post.
The waiver was needed because Barshefsky represented the Canadian lumber industry in a dispute with the United States while she was with a Washington law firm.
The swift House action reflected the wide popularity of Clinton's choice of Barshefsky as his top trade negotiator. The Senate had confirmed her by a vote of 99-1.
Clinton named Barshefsky to succeed Mickey Kantor last April. She was Kantor's deputy for three years and has been serving as acting trade representative since his departure.
Barshefsky, 46 (corrects age from 49), is known as a tough negotiator and has been praised as a vigorous advocate and defender of U.S. trade interests.
At the top of the difficult issues facing her as trade representative is the complicated U.S. relationship with China.
Barshefsky holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Wisconsin and a law degree from Catholic University in Washington.
